analysis.title: Asia Open - Open for risk
key_insights: US equities rebounded strongly on thin holiday liquidity (US cash Treasury markets closed for Veterans Day), led by the AI complex. NDX rose more than 2%.
AI rally drivers: CoreWeave beat-and-raise earnings, CoreWeave bond yields moving below 15%, OpenAI Q3 revenue of $10bn (+50% q/q vs 17% prior), and TSMC calling chip demand insatiable.
The dollar stayed well supported by Tuesday's hotter-than-expected CPI. DXY reached its highest level since May 2025.

USDJPY hit 159.82, its highest since September, just short of 160 where intervention concerns typically emerge. The Citi trader sees official action risk as less acute than the level suggests, because the yen is stronger on a trade-weighted basis than during July's intervention and the US political backdrop is potentially less sensitive.
EURUSD fell 0.70% to 1.108, its lowest level since May 2025 (the commentary also calls it an 18-month low).

G10 FX Strategy desk stays bearish AUD. A dovish RBA shift should open the way for more downside, with AUDUSD broken below 0.69 and a move toward 0.6660 in play. The desk also looks to fade bounces in EURNOK.

Crude rebounded after a sharp multi-day decline, with Brent back at $92. A WSJ report that US VP Vance is open to face-to-face talks with Iranian hardliner Rezaei capped the move. Saudi Arabia told OPEC its crude production rose 26% to one of the highest monthly levels in years.
Gold slipped below $4,000 for the first time since last week as the precious metals complex retreated further.
OIS prices a 61% chance of a rate hike in January. Treasury futures fell a few ticks, continuing Tuesday's post-CPI move.

EM and EMEA: PLN was the weakest EMEA performer with no concrete driver, and the Citi trader looks to tactically fade the move in EURPLN with a stop above the year's high at 4.4375. BRL rose 0.5% on optimism over the 2027 fiscal adjustment package, which saves 0.5% of GDP and rises to 1% and 1.25% in later years, with spending growth capped at 2%.

Calendar ahead: Japan PPI 23:50 GMT, BoJ's Asada 01:30 GMT, 5y JGB auction 03:35 GMT, UK Q3 GDP preliminary 07:00 GMT (Citi Economics expects 0.6% QoQ), ECB Economic Bulletin 09:00 GMT, Romania October CPI and NBR decision, Turkey Inflation Report 07:30 GMT, India October CPI 10:30 GMT.
earnings_insights: CoreWeave delivered a beat-and-raise earnings report (no EPS or revenue figures given in the note), which eased fears around AI demand.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Supported the dollar, took DXY to its highest since May 2025, and pushed Treasury futures lower.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets price a majority chance of a hike.
Citi Economics expects resilient growth. BoE's Pill said stalling growth could lead to a hold or cut, so downside surprises matter more.
Citi expects a rise from 6.6% in September. The NBR is expected to hold the policy rate.
Citi expects headline inflation up from 5.5% in September.

macro_indicators.indicator: Saudi crude production (as notified to OPEC)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Output rose to one of the highest monthly levels in years, adding supply pressure to crude.

trade_ideas.description: Short AUDUSD, targeting 0.6660 after the break below 0.69
trade_ideas.rationale: Dovish RBA shift should open the way for further downside as headwinds mount.
G10 FX strategists look to fade any bounces.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically fade the move in EURPLN with a stop above the year's high at 4.4375
trade_ideas.rationale: PLN weakness had no concrete driver amid thin liquidity.

risk_factors: Japanese intervention risk as USDJPY approaches 160.
Thin holiday liquidity in the US and Poland.
Hotter US inflation keeping rate-hike pricing elevated.
Middle East headline risk for crude.
Further gold weakness and dollar strength.
vol_and_positioning: Vols remained firm despite light participation, with limited upside demand.
Equity flows were mixed with some tail hedge unwinds.
CTAs will look to flip back long SPX above $7,676.
eFX desk volumes were 5% below average on the US holiday, though USDJPY and USDTHB activity surged. Net inflows skewed toward CZK, GBP, NOK and JPY, and outflows led in MXN.
geopolitical: WSJ report that US VP Vance is open to face-to-face talks with Iranian hardliner Rezaei, a de-escalatory Middle East signal that pulled crude off its highs.
Mixed Middle East headlines contributed to dollar strength and crude volatility.
